skill.name: crack-hashcat
skill.description: Guides authorized Hashcat password recovery, hash identification, attack planning, performance tuning, and reporting for security audits and forensic investigations.
skill.summary: Plan and document authorized Hashcat password audits and recovery workflows.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed critical issues around privileged system password hash extraction and remote installer piping to bash. Most other detections are documentation examples, rule templates, or reference URLs rather than executable package behavior. The skill remains high-risk because it provides dual-use password cracking workflows and handles cracked credentials.

remediation.issue: Privileged system password hash extraction examples
remediation.suggestion: Remove direct sudo reads of /etc/shadow and require offline lab hashes or safer acquisition guidance.

remediation.issue: Remote installer piped to shell in CI template
remediation.suggestion: Use a pinned release, checksum verification, or a trusted package source instead of curl pipe bash.

remediation.issue: Cracked password artifacts can be exposed
remediation.suggestion: Avoid plaintext exports and document encrypted storage, restricted permissions, retention limits, and disposal.

remediation.issue: Offensive password cracking workflows need stricter guardrails
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit refusal guidance for unauthorized hashes, live targets, and credential theft scenarios.

remediation.issue: GitHub token is passed to a third-party action
remediation.suggestion: Limit workflow token permissions and pass repository tokens only to actions that require them.

content.value_statement: Password audits need repeatable hash identification, attack selection, and reporting. This skill guides authorized Hashcat workflows for recovery, policy testing, and defensive remediation.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common hash families and maps them to Hashcat mode numbers.
Plans dictionary, mask, hybrid, and rule-based attacks for authorized hash sets.
Explains session management, performance tuning, and GPU workload choices.
Shows reporting steps for cracked and uncracked hash counts.
Connects password audit results to defensive controls and policy changes.
limitations: Does not verify legal authorization or ownership of hashes.
Does not run Hashcat by itself; users must install tools and supply hardware.
Does not safely store, encrypt, or destroy recovered passwords automatically.
Not suitable for live targets or unauthorized credential access.

use_cases.title: Run an Authorized Password Audit
use_cases.description: Plan a scoped Hashcat audit, choose attack modes, and summarize weak password patterns.

use_cases.title: Support Forensic Recovery
use_cases.description: Recover passwords from approved evidence hashes while documenting chain of custody and handling requirements.

use_cases.title: Improve Credential Controls
use_cases.description: Turn cracked password results into policy, storage, and multi-factor authentication recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Hash Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for an authorized hash sample.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have an authorized hash sample from a lab system. Help me identify likely Hashcat modes and safe next steps without exposing the secret.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Audit Attack
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a controlled password audit workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized Hashcat audit plan for these hash types and constraints. Include attack modes, resource limits, logging, and evidence handling.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Cracking Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve performance without losing control of scope.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my authorized Hashcat session settings and suggest safe tuning for workload, devices, checkpoints, and result protection.

prompt_templates.title: Write Remediation Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert audit results into defensive recommendations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a password audit findings report from these authorized results. Focus on patterns, risk, policy changes, storage controls, and MFA recommendations.

output_examples.input: An auditor asks for a first-pass plan for NTLM hashes.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends confirming scope, selecting the NTLM mode, starting with a curated wordlist, tracking success rate, and protecting outputs.

output_examples.input: A responder needs to explain weak recovered passwords.
output: Summary of cracked percentage and affected account groups.
Common patterns such as seasons, names, and short numeric suffixes.
Recommended controls including longer passphrases, blocklists, and MFA.

output_examples.input: A team needs safer handling for cracked credentials.
output_examples.output: The skill lists restricted storage, encrypted transfer, limited access, retention limits, and verified disposal steps.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before any cracking activity.
Use isolated systems and encrypt hash files, wordlists, and result artifacts.
Convert findings into password policy improvements and MFA recommendations.
anti_patterns: Cracking hashes from systems you do not own or administer.
Saving recovered passwords in shared folders, tickets, or chat logs.
Running aggressive brute force on production hardware without resource limits.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized work?
faq.answer: Yes. It is intended for approved audits, forensics, recovery, and security research with clear permission.

faq.question: Does it include Hashcat?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance. Users must install Hashcat and required GPU drivers separately.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code run the commands?
faq.answer: They can help draft commands and plans. Execution depends on the local tool permissions and user approval.

faq.question: What hash types are covered?
faq.answer: The skill references common modes such as MD5, SHA, NTLM, bcrypt, NetNTLMv2, Kerberos, and WPA formats.

faq.question: How should recovered passwords be handled?
faq.answer: Treat them as sensitive secrets. Store them encrypted, restrict access, minimize retention, and destroy them after reporting.

faq.question: Can it guarantee password recovery?
faq.answer: No. Success depends on hash strength, password complexity, wordlists, rules, hardware, and available time.
